sections.label: 1996 Protocol liability limits
sections.summary: Clauses 5 to 7 and 16 implement the 1996 Protocol, updating shipowner liability limits for maritime claims under the 1976 Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, clauses 5 to 7 and 16 implement the 1996 Protocol, which update the limits of liability of a shipowner for maritime claims covered under the 1976 International Convention on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims.

sections.label: Salvage Convention implementation clauses
sections.summary: Clauses 9, 10, 12 and 17 implement the Salvage Convention, covering reward criteria and special compensation for preventing environmental damage.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Second, clauses 9, 10, 12 and 17 implement the Salvage Convention which has the following key features: (a) the introduction of the criteria for fixing the amount of reward for salvors; (b) the introduction of a special compensation to salvors who prevented or minimised environmental damage, even if the salvage operations failed to save the ship or its cargo.

sections.label: Singapore maritime arbitration hub
sections.summary: The Bill's provisions will help Singapore maintain its position as an international maritime arbitration and dispute resolution hub.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The provisions in this Bill will help Singapore maintain our position as an international maritime arbitration and dispute resolution hub.

sections.label: Maritime conventions and law areas
sections.summary: The Bill involves three IMO conventions and two maritime law areas, bringing into force the 1989 Salvage Convention and 1996 LLMC Protocol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It involves three major International Maritime Organization (IMO) conventions and at least two major areas in maritime law, namely, the law on salvage and law on limitation of liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill proposes to bring into force some key maritime conventions of the world: the Salvage Convention of 1989 and the 1996 Protocol to the Convention on Limitation of Liability to the Maritime Claims (LLMC) of 1976.

sections.label: 2012 tonnage limits increase
sections.summary: On 12 April 2012, member states agreed to a roughly 51% increase in tonnage limits from 8 June 2015 to reflect monetary values and inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On 12 April 2012, the member states to the 1996 Protocol agreed to an increase of approximately 51% in tonnage limits in their jurisdictions with effect from 8 June 2015 to reflect the changes of monetary values over the period and to cope with inflation.

sections.label: 2012 amendment in UK and Hong Kong
sections.summary: For Singapore, the 2012 amendment was brought into force in the UK in 2016 and in Hong Kong on 4 December 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Significantly, for Singapore, the 2012 amendment was brought into force in the UK in 2016 and in Hong Kong on 4 December 2017.

sections.label: Fair rate environmental salvage decision
sections.summary: It was decided that the term "fair rate" in Article 14 for environmental salvage covers only expenditure, without an element of profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Essentially, it was decided that the term "fair rate" in Article 14 for environmental salvage only cover expenditure but does not include an element of profit.

sections.label: South Africa Wreck and Salvage Act
sections.summary: South Africa's Wreck and Salvage Act 1996 incorporated the Salvage Convention but differs on Article 14 special compensation and the "fair rate".

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: South Africa's Wreck and Salvage Act 1996 incorporated the Salvage Convention into their domestic law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the Act differs from the Salvage Convention in two important respects, one of which is that in relation to Article 14 on special compensation, "damage to the environment" is extended to any place where the damage may occur and the "fair rate", as referred to in Article 14, is deemed to include an element of profit.

sections.label: SCMA arbitration clause in BIMCO
sections.summary: In 2012, SCMA persuaded BIMCO to include Singapore and SCMA's arbitration clause as BIMCO's third standard dispute resolution clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2012, SCMA managed to persuade the Baltic and International Maritime Council (BIMCO), the world largest shipping association and also the world's leading generator of standard maritime contracts, to include Singapore and SCMA's arbitration clause as BIMCO's third standard dispute resolution clause, after London and New York, for world shipping contract form precedents.

sections.label: Timing of 1996 Protocol accession
sections.summary: Singapore had not previously acceded to the 1996 Protocol as the industry had concerns over increased shipowners' liability limits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: To address Mr Dennis Tan's query on the timing of accession to the 1996 Protocol, Singapore had not previously done so as the industry had some concerns with the increase in shipowners' liability limits.

sections.label: Accession to 1996 Protocol benefits
sections.summary: Accession to the 1996 Protocol will promote Singapore law and attract claimants, and Singapore will adopt liability limits increased by 50% in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Accession to the 1996 Protocol will also promote the selection of Singapore law as the governing law of commercial shipping contracts and attract more claimants to utilise our legal and arbitration dispute facilities and services, advancing our position as a leading maritime dispute resolution hub.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I am glad to inform Mr Dennis Tan that Singapore will adopt the existing liability limits which were, in 2012, increased by 50% over the original 1996 Protocol limits.

sections.label: Profit element and Salvage Convention compromises
sections.summary: Legislating an additional profit element could upset the Salvage Convention's compromises, and the Bill will maintain Singapore's competitiveness as an international maritime centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Legislating an additional profit element could potentially upset the intricate compromises upon which the Salvage Convention was built.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This Bill will enable Singapore to maintain our competitiveness as an international maritime centre.
